summary: Staggered KV warmup causing intermittent p99 latency spikes for repeat prompts
description: Issue summary: Customer reports that repeated conversational prompts (short turns repeated 3-6x) are experiencing intermittent p99 latency spikes and occasional request timeouts. Impact: Production degradation for several API routes; some user sessions see 1-2s baseline latency jump to >6s p99 and a small number of 504/timeout errors. Environment: Dedicated pool for NovelDocs in us-east, pinned to redwood-compat-7b model, steady qps ~60. Observed at 2026-03-10 15:20 UTC and recurring during next hours. This appears tied to how the KV/prefix cache warmup and shard prefetch are scheduled under client burst patterns, causing staggered cache population and head-of-line waits for repeat-context requests.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use NovelDocs prod-mimic workload: repeat a short 30-token prompt 4x with 100ms inter-turn gap
2) Target the dedicated pool us-east pinned to redwood-compat-7b
3) Observe latency distribution across sequential turns; watch p50/p90/p99 and any 504s
4) Repeat with concurrency of 3 clients to simulate real traffic bursts
logs: 2026-03-10T15:24:03Z serving-runtime: request id 7bfa2a - prefix lookup miss -> kv-prefetch scheduled (shard 12)
2026-03-10T15:24:03Z scheduler: prefetch worker queued (worker=3) for shard 12, expected start delay 120ms
2026-03-10T15:24:04Z serving-runtime: request id 7bfa2b - blocked waiting for KV fill for same prefix, observed wait 630ms
2026-03-10T15:24:05Z api-gateway: proxied request 504 to client after backend timeout 5000ms
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: KV cache cold fills are being serialized per-shard and prefetch tasks are intentionally staggered to avoid thundering herd; this interacts poorly with repeat short-turn conversational traffic, creating head-of-line waits for subsequent turns that hit the same prefix.

Observed pattern: p99 spikes coincide with interleaved prefetch scheduling where worker concurrency is limited (prefetch_worker_limit=3) and shard prioritization uses FIFO across shards; when multiple simultaneous short-turn sessions touch same shard, one request triggers a prefetch while others queue awaiting the cache fill.
Heap/profile: No memory OOMs. Prefetch worker pool shows saturation with backlog during the spike windows. CPU/GPU utilization normal. Disk/IO latencies nominal.
Reproduced in staging by lowering prefetch_worker_limit to 2 and creating 3 concurrent clients doing repeated short prompts; p99 spikes reproduced reliably.

Compared to baseline: previous routing allowed speculative concurrent prefetches for the same prefix (race-y) which reduced latency but caused slight extra KV load; the recent change to serialize per-prefix prefetch removed duplicate fills but exposed blocking for repeat prompts.

Check related config change: Deploy abc1234 (scheduler) rolled out 2026-03-08 changed prefetch serialization logic and introduced per-shard FIFO prioritization. Related PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/4821

root_cause: Prefetch scheduling change (per-shard FIFO + strict per-prefix serialization) created head-of-line blocking for repeat short-turn prompts in dedicated pools. The serialization prevented bounded speculative concurrent fills for the same prefix, so subsequent repeat turns waited for a single fill to complete, causing p99 latency spikes and occasional timeouts.
resolution: Temporary mitigation: Enabled customer-scoped feature flag 'kv_allow_speculative_fills' for NovelDocs (2026-03-12) which allowed bounded concurrent fills for identical prefixes and restored latency to baseline. Long-term fix: Deploy PR 4838 which adjusts scheduler to prioritize in-flight prefix prefetches and allow controlled speculative fills when route marked latency-sensitive. Full rollout scheduled 2026-03-14 after 24h canary.
